subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped dry-run security contract should OpenClaw expose for agent tool execution across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, code mode, and hooks?
rationale: This feature would be a user-trusted no-side-effects boundary, and current source has multiple execution paths where process-global or partial interception could be unsafe.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, code-mode, and deferred-tool paths.

options.title: Fold into broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this blocked until Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode chooses the shared vocabulary and safety guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep only scoped command-level dry-runs if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misunderstand as a full sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify CLI and runtime semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, code-mode, and deferred-tool paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-source and history signal for the agent tool adapter and CLI registration surfaces involved in the decision.
